coordinates.object_orientation: Head -Y, abdomen +Y, dorsal +Z, wings spread left/right.

concept.reason: Viewed real named holotype, primary complete reconstruction and dimensional description.

scope: Complete Carboniferous winged insect with robust thorax, two broad-based tapered flight-wing pairs and paired small prothoracic winglets. Genus-level female interpretation anchored to S.lobata specimen22-1, current museum holotype MNHN.F.R51415, with explicitly attributed comparative completion from Kukalova1970.

scientific_limits.en: Not a single-specimen scan or certain whole S.lobata individual: genus composite follows the published1970 reconstruction. Wing66×17.5mm and abdomen39mm are published lobata measurements; missing beak, legs, winglet outline, distal palps and ovipositor use separately identified comparative evidence. Depth, color, posture and unseen distal proportions remain inferred.
scientific_limits.zh: 非单标本扫描或确定保存完整的lobata个体，而是明确沿用1970论文的属级组合复原。前翅66×17.5毫米、腹长39毫米为lobata发表数据；缺损口器、足、前胸翼叶轮廓、须末端及产卵器使用分别标明的比较来源。厚度、颜色、姿态及未保存远端比例为推断。

taxon: Stenodictya sp. (genus-level reconstruction anchored to S.lobata female holotype)

scale.uncertainty: Body length sums measured segments plus estimated prothorax; cerci full length and depth not preserved measurements. Use actual wing dimensions, not generic giant-insect maximum.

anatomy: Two large flight-wing pairs attached to meso/metathorax, widest near base then markedly narrowing in apical third. Hindwings slightly wider; major vein branches plus simplified crossvein network, not arbitrary dragonfly needles.
Paired cordate prothoracic lobes anterior to flight wings, about two-thirds forewing width, fan-like vein relief. These are small winglets, not a third equal flight pair or dorsal shield.
Small head with broad clypeal region, pair of eyes and antennae, forward/downward sucking beak with paired palps. Do not replace with chewing beetle mandibles.

Three thoracic segments with median grooves, robust sculpted dorsal cuticle; abdomen slightly broader than thorax, overlapping transverse tergites with modest pointed posterolateral corners and oblique strengthening ridges. No free gill paddles.
Three pairs of short articulated legs, five-part tarsal construction and tiny claws. Limbs arranged so wing bases do not hide every leg in all views.

Female-mode tail: pair of long tapering robust cerci and a modest separate curved ovipositor. Never add spinosa male claspers to lobata-based female. Cerci length and ovipositor distal completion explicitly inferred.
restoration_boundaries: Actual MNHN.F.R51415 museum photograph viewed, showing body and wings in slab; repository record gives lobata holotype and same taxonomic history as Brongniart22-1. Photo is real fossil, not reconstructed anatomy.
Kukalova1970 Fig51 and p12 fix lobata22-1 head, main wings, thorax, abdomen and female terminal bases. Published66×17.5mmforewing,39mmabdomen,7.8/7.2mmthorax.
Fig50 is explicitly a genus composite, NOT actual fossil: S.pygmaea winglet outline; S.oustaleti/S.agnita legs and five-segment tarsi; S.laurentiauxi beak.

Original author used other palaeodictyopterans to estimate incomplete structures: Eugereon palpal length, broader group labrum, Homaloneura ovipositor length. Keep these as approximate functional completion, not species diagnosis or directly measured lobata features.

Handlirsch/Sharov popular reconstructions were criticized in revision. Avoid dorsal shield mistaken from ventral view, broad untapered wings, exaggerated free abdominal gills and mixed male/female genitalia.
The model fulfills original complete genus-level gate; it does not assert a definitive modern phylogenetic interpretation of abdominal expansions. Color, body thickness and flight pose artistic.
quality_gates: Whole winged insect with robust thorax, two flight pairs and two small prothoracic lobes.
66mm tapered forewing proportions; no replacement with broad featureless rectangles.
Female tail with paired cerci, no spinosa male claspers; no external abdominal gills.
Three leg pairs, two antennae and separate sucking mouthparts.
Public limitations preserve explicit genus composite and partwise evidence; four fixedviews only.
